title: Deploying a skill to canvas marks a materially stickier user than merely creating one — deployers retain 43%/27% (wk1/wk4) vs creators 36%/20%, gap WIDENING; but no credit-monetization premium
one_liner: Directly answering the Jul-16 open backlog question — do skill DEPLOYERS (skill_used = 'Skill Added to Canvas') retain/monetize better than create-only users? — the answer on ENGAGEMENT retention is a clear YES, and the gap WIDENS over time. On matched weekly retention curves (prod, births Jun 16-Jul 13 2026 — the window where BOTH events carry real volume, since skill_used was only instrumented ~Jun 16), users cohorted on their first skill DEPLOY return to agent messaging at 42.6% wk1 (86/202) and 27.2% wk4 (55/202), vs users cohorted on their first skill CREATE at 36.0% wk1 (127/353) and 19.5% wk4 (69/353) — a 1.18x wk1 and 1.40x wk4 deploy premium that grows with tenure. Because deployers are a ~23% SUBSET of creators (Jul-16), the create-ONLY sub-population retains BELOW the 36% blended creator rate, so the true deploy-vs-create-only gap is LARGER than the 43-vs-36 blended contrast. So the create->deploy step (the 77-88% leak sized on Jul-16) is not a cosmetic milestone — the ~1 in 4 creators who actually drag a skill onto the canvas are the materially stickier cohort, and the widening wk4 gap says deployment marks durable, not just transient, engagement. The MONETIZATION half is the honest counterweight: there is NO measurable deploy premium on credit top-ups — deployers converted 3/184 (1.6%) to a credit_topup within 30d vs creators 24/664 (3.6%), and the deployer N=3 is far too small to call a real difference — so the deploy advantage lives on retained product usage, not on (pre-settlement) credit monetization. Marks not drives: deployers by construction took MORE actions (created AND deployed), so reverse causation (already-committed users deploy) is at least as likely as deployment itself causing the retention.

title: Deep builders are a NESTED subset of deep conversers, not a disjoint population — 68% of top-decile building companies are also top-decile conversers, but only 23% the reverse (build ⊂ converse)
one_liner: Answering the backlog question directly -- do the ~10% power-user cores on node_used (BUILD) and agent_message_sent (CONVERSE) overlap at company grain, or are builders and conversers disjoint account sets? -- the answer is NEITHER disjoint NOR symmetric: deep building is a NESTED INNER CORE inside the broader conversation population. On per-company total-event distributions (prod, last 90d, company_id $user profile; node 1,033 companies / 18,188 attributed node-adds, agent 2,988 companies / ~29,549 msgs), 68.0% of top-decile building companies (70/103) are ALSO top-decile conversing companies, and 95% (98/103) send at least one agent message -- i.e. almost every deep builder is also a deep (or at least active) converser. The REVERSE is weak and asymmetric: only 23.4% of top-decile conversing companies (70/299) are also top-decile builders, and only 78% of them add any node at all -- most deep conversers never build deeply. The same nesting holds at the top 1% (elite): 60% of the 10 build-elite are agent-elite vs only 20% of the 30 agent-elite are build-elite. At the ANY-activity level the asymmetry repeats -- of 1,033 companies that build, 789 (76%) also converse; of 2,988 that converse, only 789 (26%) also build. And the volume mirrors it: the 789 dual-active companies hold 92.6% of ALL node-adds but only 68.1% of all agent messages -- building volume lives almost entirely inside dual-active accounts, while ~32% of conversation volume sits in a chat-ONLY tail (2,199 companies, 74% of all conversers, that never add a single node). Correlation confirms the shape: across the union (0-fill, N=3,232) Spearman rho is only 0.148 -- dragged down by the huge chat-only tail -- but AMONG the 789 companies that do both, log-log Pearson r = 0.545 (moderate: once a company builds at all, its build depth and chat depth rise together). Net reframe of the Aug-5 power-law: builders and conversers are not two separate power-user populations -- the build core is a strict, deeper subset (build ⊂ converse). Sizing the leak (today's twist): ~2,200 companies engage the assistant purely via chat and never touch the canvas builder -- the single biggest untapped 'converse-but-never-build' pool -- vs only 244 companies that build without conversing. Marks not drives: heavy builders by construction do more of everything, so the nesting reflects an engaged inner core, not that building causes conversing.

title: Landing context measurably marks signup conversion -- homepage arm home_a beats home_b 37% vs 32% (onboarding->signup, p~.03) and template-arrivals convert ~2x; both arms sit below the untagged direct-entry path (52%)
one_liner: Directly answering today's assigned angle -- does the landing context (home_variant / has_template) captured at onboarding_started change signup conversion? -- and giving the homepage A/B experiment its first actual per-arm CONVERSION read (the ledger has only ever logged the Jul-3 collapse DROPS by variant, never the completion RATE). On the only clean month the experiment has (June 2026: home_a/home_b launched in June -- all of May was 'undefined' -- and July 3 collapsed the funnel, so June is the single measurable window), onboarding_started->signup_completed (prod, unique, 1-day window) splits three ways: home_a completes 36.9% (314/850), home_b 32.1% (350/1,089), and the UNTAGGED/'undefined' entry path 52.3% (1,015/1,939), against a 43.9% blended baseline (1,674/3,813). Two clean reads. (1) The A/B answer: home_a beats home_b by 4.8pp = a 15% relative lift, and it is statistically real (z=2.21, p~=0.027) -- so landing context DOES move conversion, and the currently-split traffic is leaving the weaker arm live. (2) The uncomfortable one: BOTH experiment arms convert well BELOW the untagged path (52%). That is most likely a confound, not proof the homepage hurts -- 'undefined' is not a randomized control but whoever was never bucketed into the experiment (plausibly higher-intent direct/SSO/deep-link entry that skips the marketing homepage, consistent with the ~52% matching May's pre-experiment 48% baseline) -- so read it as 'the homepage-experiment cohort converts lower than the direct-entry cohort', which marks WHO lands on the homepage, not that the page is worse. Sizing the leak (today's twist), on June volumes: shipping home_a's rate to all home_b traffic recovers ~52 signups/month (the clean, actionable number -- kill home_b); if you instead (loosely) held the arms to the untagged 52% path the gap is ~351 signups/month, but that upper bound is confounded by the entry-route selection above. The has_template facet points the same way, harder but on tiny N: the ~1% of onboarding_started that arrive WITH a template pre-selected (has_template=true) complete signup at 78.4% (29/37) vs 43.6% (1,645/3,776) without -- ~1.8x -- consistent with the ledger's template-intent-marks-committed-users theme, but N=37 so directional only. Net: the assigned angle resolves YES -- landing context measurably marks conversion (home_a>home_b, significant; template-arrivals ~2x) -- with the actionable move being to retire the losing home_b arm (~52 signups/mo) and the honest caveat that the arms-vs-untagged gap is an entry-route selection effect, not a proven homepage penalty. Marks not drives.
angle: home_variant / has_template at onboarding_started: does landing context change conversion? -- per-variant onboarding->signup completion (the A/B arms' actual conversion rate, never before measured) + within-experiment leak sizing
confidence: medium (home_a vs home_b N=850/1089, z=2.21 p~.03, solid; has_template N=37 directional; arms-vs-untagged confounded by entry route)
caveat: Mixpanel funnel onboarding_started->signup_completed, prod (environment=='production'), countType=unique, 1-day conversion window, breakdown by the EVENT-level home_variant / has_template captured on the onboarding_started entry event. Window = June 1-30 2026, the ONLY clean measurable month: home_a/home_b were instrumented starting June (a May breakdown returns 100% 'undefined' = 8,123->48%, i.e. the experiment did not exist yet), and the Jul-3 signup collapse (ledger Aug-6/Jul-20: signup_completed floored ~-92%, onboarding_started ~-67/-80%) makes any July+ window unusable -- so the assigned 'by signup-cohort month' lens cannot be run (one clean month only). Bases: overall 3,813->1,674 (43.9%); undefined 1,939->1,015 (52.3%); home_b 1,089->350 (32.1%); home_a 850->314 (36.9%). home_a vs home_b two-proportion z=2.21, p~=0.027 (significant); N per arm 850/1,089 is solid. KEY CONFOUND: 'undefined'/untagged is NOT a randomized control -- it is onboarding_started events with no home_variant assigned (plausibly direct/SSO/deep-link entry that bypasses the marketing homepage), and it converts at 52% ~= May's pre-experiment 48% baseline, so the arms-below-untagged gap is most likely an entry-route SELECTION effect, not a homepage penalty; the robust causal-flavored contrast is the within-experiment home_a vs home_b (both are homepage arms, so the 15% lift is a fair A/B read). has_template=true N=37 (29 completers) is small -- 78.4% is directional, not bankable; has_template=true also sits almost entirely under home_variant=undefined so it is not a clean cross of the two facets. 1-day window slightly under-counts late completers (would lift all rates a little, not change the ranking). Unit is distinct_id, NOT company_id-deduped. Leak sizing applies June rates: ~52 signups/mo recoverable by moving home_b traffic to home_a (clean); ~351/mo vs the untagged path (confounded upper bound). Extends the Aug-7 channel-completion finding (same funnel/window, different splitter: utm channel) and closes the Jul-20 'home_variant angle unanswerable until the funnel is restored' note by answering it on the pre-collapse June data instead of waiting for a recovery that hasn't come.
